items.title: Hate generative AI? Maybe it's time to boycott Netflix
items.excerpt: With Netflix leaning into generative AI across its productions, Creative Bloq argues creatives angry about AI's encroachment on craft should vote with their subscriptions. It's a look at how a major studio's gen-AI adoption reshapes creative and design work and the leverage audiences and practitioners still hold — a culture-and-craft read on the design/creative industry's AI backlash.

items.title: Full-Body, Hand & Facial Motion Capture From Any Video In Blender
items.excerpt: Arcomade's BlendCap is a locally-run AI motion-capture add-on that tracks body, hands, and face from a single recorded video and retargets the performance onto character rigs inside Blender — no markers, motion suit, subscription, or internet connection required after install. It brings AI-driven performance capture into a mainstream 3D/design tool with built-in presets for popular rigging systems, lowering the barrier for animators and product/3D designers.

items.title: From feedback to merged PR: making UI feedback agent-actionable
items.excerpt: As teams wire AI coding agents (Cursor, Claude) into implementation, the shape of design feedback has to change: notes captured directly on the live app with page URLs, element selectors, screenshots, and viewport context can be converted straight into pull requests without a human translation step. A concrete look at agentic design-to-code handoff — how design critique becomes machine-actionable rather than a Figma comment or Slack thread.

items.title: Why Do AI-Generated Websites All Look the Same?
items.excerpt: AI website builders now ship clean, responsive code, yet the output converges on the same visual signatures — glassmorphism, identical hero layouts, standardized card grids. The piece argues models reproduce common patterns rather than truly design, a pointed 'AI slop' critique of homogenized generative UI and what it means for brand differentiation and design taste.
